title: Fix `team_drive_update` forwarding and `is_mine` for ownerless resources
description:
### `team_drive_update()` errored on every call

The deprecated `team_drive_update()` forwarded to `shared_drive_update()` under the wrong argument name

`shared_drive_update()` has formals `(shared_drive, ...)`, so `drive = team_drive` landed in `...` and the required `shared_drive` was
missing. Every call errored before doing anything.

### `is_mine()` errors for resources without an owner

`is_mine()` plucks `owners[[1]]$me` out of each `drive_resource`. Resources without owners, such as shared drives, make that pluck return zero elements and `map_lgl()` errors

```r
res <- list(
  list(kind = "drive#file", owners = list(list(me = TRUE))),
  list(kind = "drive#file")
)
map_lgl(res, list("owners", 1, "me"))
#> Error:
#> ! In index: 2.
#> Caused by error:
#> ! Result must be length 1, not 0.
```

Found during my most recent [ry](https://github.com/sims1253/ry) audit.

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Update file types supported by `drive_download()`
description:
Since Google Docs now [supports exporting to Markdown](https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2024/07/import-and-export-markdown-in-google-docs.html), it seemed like a good idea to enable that support in `drive_download()`.

The only code I changed manually was to add the default `.md` extension for `text/markdown` mimetype in `data-raw/extension-mime-type-defaults.csv`. Then I just ran `data-raw/mime-types.R` to pull in the Google MIME types and create the csv files in `inst/extdata/data/`.

This does work now:

``` r
library(googledrive)

drive_auth(email = "andy@andyteucher.ca")

drive_download(
  "https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EK6WZyEUfdy6sj3GjLII20Ok7qTcmRD-vv-osfHnkPU",
  path = "my_document.md",
)
#> File downloaded:
#> • 'Test for google drive' <id: 1EK6WZyEUfdy6sj3GjLII20Ok7qTcmRD-vv-osfHnkPU>
#> Saved locally as:
#> • 'my_document.md'
```

title: Modernize the warn_for_verbose() helper
description:
The motivation for this update is that I will probably feature this as a "deprecation helper" in R Packages. I.e. the type of thing one might do if a deprecation affects a lot of code, such as when googledrive deprecated the `verbose` argument present in virtually every single function in favour of an option.

The helper has been here for quite a while, so I'm updating it to remove some DIY moves and be more idiomatic with modern lifecycle.

How it gets used in almost every function in googledrive:

``` r
drive_create <- function(name,
                         path = NULL,
                         type = NULL,
                         ...,
                         overwrite = NA,
                         verbose = deprecated()) {
  warn_for_verbose(verbose)
  ...
}
```

title: Implement `drive_id` class more fully
description:
Closes #93 

*Some aspects of this PR were done in a certain way, in order to generate discussion for a live code review in a group meeting*

---

googledrive has always had `drive_id`, a lightweight S3 class to mark a string (or character vector) as file ID, instead of a filename.

`drive_id` pre-dated vctrs and was implemented in a very minimal way.

Overall, it’s been OK, but there are annoying downsides:

-   File IDs are almost meaningless to humans, but they take up lots of valuable
    space when printing `dribble`s, often at the expense of `name`, which is
    often more interesting to the user.
-   Any sort of manipulation tends to lose the `drive_id` class.
-   You can put strings in a `drive_id` object that are definitely not valid, like
    `""`.

Here’s what I mean:

``` r
drive_find(n_max = 3)
#> # A dribble: 3 x 3
#>   name                        id                                   drive_resource  
#> * <chr>                       <chr>                                <list>          
#> 1 foo_sheet-TEST-drive_publi… 1CEefQCUc5T7B4yrawnNfqwdWEbiDyDs9E5… <named list [36…
#> 2 foo_doc-TEST-drive_publish  1oUrQNg-2lcAieZyCqoQ_vDwYLMVzhN4-oO… <named list [36…
#> 3 imdb_latin1_csv-TEST-drive… 1o_7f6WRXN-CxgijwgfpDiust8A3zKcNI    <named list [39…

(ids <- as_id(month.abb))
#>  [1] "Jan" "Feb" "Mar" "Apr" "May" "Jun" "Jul" "Aug" "Sep" "Oct" "Nov" "Dec"
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "drive_id"
just_two <- ids[c(2, 5)]
just_two
#> [1] "Feb" "May"
class(just_two)
#> [1] "character"

as_id(c("", "lskdjflslsei"))
#> [1] ""             "lskdjflslsei"
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "drive_id"
```

This PR implements `drive_id` more fully and uses the capabilities in vctrs and pillar to address the above.
Resources consulted:

-   [S3 chapter of Advanced R](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/s3.html)
-   [S3 vectors vignette in vctrs](https://vctrs.r-lib.org/articles/s3-vector.html)
-   [Printing vectors nicely in tibbles vignette in vctrs](https://vctrs.r-lib.org/articles/pillar.html)

Another relevant resource is [Davis’s notes](https://github.com/DavisVaughan/2020-06-01_dplyr-vctrs-compat) on
“adding dplyr and vctrs support to your tibble subclass so that it works with the tidyverse”.
I recently updated the technology behind the `dribble` subclass and, since the `id` column of a `dribble` should be a `drive_id` (but previously was not), these two efforts intersect.

TL;DR here’s how things work now:

*The final `drive_id` truncation strategy ended up being different. There is less truncation than shown here.*

``` r
dat <- drive_find("jenny", n_max = 5)
dat
#> # A dribble: 5 x 3
#>   name                                         id       drive_resource   
#>   <chr>                                        <drv_id> <list>           
#> 1 DESCRIPTION-TEST-drive_upload-jenny-8fb0b018 19TUFZL… <named list [40]>
#> 2 DESC-TEST-drive_mv-jenny-9db391f6            1YbwaJe… <named list [40]>
#> 3 DESC-TEST-drive_mv-jenny-4be97296            18wab1k… <named list [40]>
#> 4 DESC-TEST-drive_mv-jenny-4be97296            1IH6z0z… <named list [40]>
#> 5 DESC-TEST-drive_mv-jenny-b4c90052            1qQMpEJ… <named list [40]>

(ids <- as_id(month.abb))
#> <drive_id[12]>
#>  [1] Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec
just_two <- ids[c(2, 5)]
just_two
#> <drive_id[2]>
#> [1] Feb May
class(just_two)
#> [1] "drive_id"   "vctrs_vctr"

as_id(c("", "lskdjflslsei"))
#> Error: A <drive_id> must match this regular expression: `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`
#> Invalid input:
#> x '""'
```

## Problems and observations

The `pillar::pillar_shaft()` method isn’t working how I want.
Current work-around is to always truncate the `drive_id`s in a tibble.
This is not great, because sometimes you really do need access to the whole id for copy/paste. <https://github.com/r-lib/pillar/issues/331>

*That 👆 was resolved by settling for the truncation normally done on `character` columns. It's not ideal but it's better than nothing.*

~Lots of `as.character(id)` is necessary when incorporating `drive_id`s into requests, because of:~

``` r
ids
#> <drive_id[12]>
#>  [1] Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec
jsonlite::toJSON(ids)
#> Error: No method asJSON S3 class: vctrs_vctr
```

*That 👆 was resolved by inheriting base class (character) in `new_drive_id()`.*

title: Add `drive_read()`
description:
Closes #81 

*Some aspects of this PR are deliberately undone or done a certain way, in order to generate discussion when we do live code review in a group meeting*

Adds `drive_read()` which is sort of like:
`drive_download("path/to/local/file")` + `read_WHATEVER("path/to/local/file")`
But without doing the download, i.e. no local file is ever created.

I don't think comes up much, but I have occasionally wanted this myself and it's a long-standing issue/request. It was definitely time to do it or close it.

Key points to notice or discuss:

* If I add `drive_read()`, what does that imply re: the inverse `drive_write()`? I already closed that issue as "won't do", but it usually makes sense to implement both members of such a pair. https://github.com/tidyverse/googledrive/issues/44
* I don't want to do much parsing, e.g. re-implement the now-regretted `httr::content(as = "parsed")`. My goal is to shoot for exposing [httr2's body processing functions](https://httr2.r-lib.org/reference/resp_body_raw.html). Fully? Partially?
* I've stowed lots of examples that were useful in development as actual examples, but I can't leave them there. What to do with code like that?
* In hindsight, it's no surprise, but there were, of course, some encoding issues to address.

---

Here's how it looks in action.

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/rrr/googledrive")
#> ℹ Loading googledrive

# plain text --> character vector
r_desc <- system.file("DESCRIPTION") %>%
  drive_upload()
#> Local file:
#> • '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/library/base/DESCRIPTION'
#> Uploaded into Drive file:
#> • 'DESCRIPTION' <id: 11VZd0MvsPwPCo8M0OJPF9PzHzC8rGKbW>
#> With MIME type:
#> • 'text/plain'
r_desc %>%
  drive_read() %>%
  readr::read_lines()
#> ℹ MIME type of body: 'text/plain'
#> ℹ Setting `as = "string"`
#> No encoding supplied: defaulting to UTF-8.
#>  [1] "Package: base"                                                 
#>  [2] "Version: 4.1.0"                                                
#>  [3] "Priority: base"                                                
#>  [4] "Title: The R Base Package"                                     
#>  [5] "Author: R Core Team and contributors worldwide"                
#>  [6] "Maintainer: R Core Team <do-use-Contact-address@r-project.org>"
#>  [7] "Contact: R-help mailing list <r-help@r-project.org>"           
#>  [8] "Description: Base R functions."                                
#>  [9] "License: Part of R 4.1.0"                                      
#> [10] "Suggests: methods"                                             
#> [11] "Built: R 4.1.0; ; 2021-05-19 20:55:40 UTC; unix"

drive_rm(r_desc)
#> File deleted:
#> • 'DESCRIPTION' <id: 11VZd0MvsPwPCo8M0OJPF9PzHzC8rGKbW>

# comma-separated values --> tibble
chicken_csv <- drive_example("chicken.csv") %>%
  drive_upload()
#> Local file:
#> • '/Users/jenny/rrr/googledrive/inst/extdata/chicken.csv'
#> Uploaded into Drive file:
#> • 'chicken.csv' <id: 1rebNEHrAmR14iTVKfk2kX2W-aWixzgoP>
#> With MIME type:
#> • 'text/csv'
chicken_csv %>%
  drive_read() %>%
  readr::read_csv()
#> ℹ MIME type of body: 'text/csv'
#> ℹ Setting `as = "string"`
#> No encoding supplied: defaulting to UTF-8.
#> # A tibble: 5 x 4
#>   chicken            breed         sex    motto                                 
#>   <chr>              <chr>         <chr>  <chr>                                 
#> 1 Foghorn Leghorn    Leghorn       roost… That's a joke, ah say, that's a joke,…
#> 2 Chicken Little     unknown       hen    The sky is falling!                   
#> 3 Ginger             Rhode Island… hen    Listen. We'll either die free chicken…
#> 4 Camilla the Chick… Chantecler    hen    Bawk, buck, ba-gawk.                  
#> 5 Ernie The Giant C… Brahma        roost… Put Captain Solo in the cargo hold.

drive_rm("chicken.csv")
#> File deleted:
#> • 'chicken.csv' <id: 1rebNEHrAmR14iTVKfk2kX2W-aWixzgoP>

# Google Doc --> character vector
chicken_doc <- drive_example("chicken.txt") %>%
  drive_upload(type = "document")
#> Local file:
#> • '/Users/jenny/rrr/googledrive/inst/extdata/chicken.txt'
#> Uploaded into Drive file:
#> • 'chicken' <id: 1wHSOlxWP13l-UFOu9UINjlR9C5ZYfUXykI3Jn3bU0d8>
#> With MIME type:
#> • 'application/vnd.google-apps.document'
chicken_doc %>%
  # NOTE: we must specify an export MIME type
  drive_read(type = "text/plain") %>%
  strsplit(split = "(\r\n|\r|\n)") %>%
  .[[1]]
#> ℹ MIME type of body: 'text/plain'
#> ℹ Setting `as = "string"`
#> No encoding supplied: defaulting to UTF-8.
#> [1] "A chicken whose name was Chantecler"      
#> [2] "Clucked in iambic pentameter"             
#> [3] "It sat on a shelf, reading Song of Myself"
#> [4] "And laid eggs with a perfect diameter."   
#> [5] ""                                         
#> [6] ""                                         
#> [7] "—Richard Maxson"

drive_rm(chicken_doc)
#> File deleted:
#> • 'chicken' <id: 1wHSOlxWP13l-UFOu9UINjlR9C5ZYfUXykI3Jn3bU0d8>

# JPEG --> raw --> raster
# https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-patched/doc/html/logo.jpg
r_logo <- R.home("doc/html/logo.jpg") %>%
  drive_upload(name = "r_logo.jpg")
#> Local file:
#> • '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/doc/html/logo.jpg'
#> Uploaded into Drive file:
#> • 'r_logo.jpg' <id: 10-RIAFanZD1SviUA69Lmo0Xb-iPGDX6s>
#> With MIME type:
#> • 'image/jpeg'
img <- r_logo %>%
  drive_read() %>%
  jpeg::readJPEG()
#> ℹ MIME type of body: 'image/jpeg'
#> ℹ Setting `as = "raw"`
plot(0:1, 0:1, type = "n")
rasterImage(img, 0, 0, 1, 1)
```

title: Stop worrying about multiple parent folders
description:
Closes #356

The docs linked in #356 make this task look more complicated than it seems to be. That is, if the user is trying to do a move they aren't permitted to do, I am happy for them to see an error. I have no ambitions to parse the `capabilities` and try to intercept a request that will fail. Based on personal experience, the value of these `capabilities` and the real-world significance of different values is pretty hard to predict anyway. Want to move a file? Just try it and see what happens.

title: Fix for garbled multibyte Google Sheets title in drive_upload
description:
## Issue to resolve
On Windows, when uploading a CSV file as a Google Sheets spreadsheet with a sheet title that includes multibyte characters, the title of the resulting uploaded spreadsheet is garbled.

e.g.
```
googledrive::drive_upload(csv_filepath, "Title with multibyte - マルチバイトのタイトル", type = "spreadsheet", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## Cause
This is because of unnecessary encoding translation done by writeLines(), which writes the JSON content to the temporary file for subsequent HTTP upload request. The content of the written JSON file gets garbled. 

## Fix
To avoid the unnecessary encoding translation, I added useBytes = TRUE argument to the writeLines call.
Reference: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10675360/utf-8-file-output-in-r

## Test
Tested that this resolves the garbling issue on Windows, and also drive_upload keeps working on Mac.

## R CMD check results
```

Duration: 1m 3.9s

    'drive_set_token'
```

title: Deprecate `verbose`; introduce googledrive_quiet option
description:
I'm happy with how this works, but am inviting review of a very specific aspect (I comment this inline): how I determine the name of the calling function.

Big picture: googledrive had a `verbose` argument in 26 user-facing functions. I'm removing that, in favour of an option. I don't think many people actually need or want to fiddle with verbosity at the level of individual function calls. Very few users want to fiddle with verbosity at all, I imagine.

I want to wrap `lifecycle::deprecate_warn()` (i.e. use a shared `id`) and then call it from all 26 functions.

`warn_for_verbose()` catches the rare use of `drive_something(..., verbose = FALSE)`, warns, suggests what to do in future, and calls `local_drive_quiet()`.

title: Update link, add note on invalidity of inputs within examples.
description:
- [x] Proofread title, description, and parameters
- [x] Proofread comments in examples
- [x] Ensure comment headings used to divide into scannable sections
- [x] Flag examples that seem overly complex for further review
- [x] ~~Switch out mtcars/iris for something more interesting, or a smaller dataset constructed specifically to illustrate one point.~~
- [x] Review size of example outputs to ensure that you can easily see important rows and cols.
- [x] ~~Datasets should always be tibbles to avoid use of as_tibble() distracting from the main point~~

Checks are what I did, strikethroughs do not seem relevant to the issue. 

### Summary of changes:

* Update a link in `@seealso` to point to the `files.get` endpoint link instead of `files.update`. This seems to be correct because in the preceding text it references files.get/list, not files.update/list.

* Add a note at the top of the examples indicating many will return 0-row tibbles or error unless the function inputs are replaced with paths or ids which exist on the user's Drive.

### Questions:

The return value of the function is shared through a template, which says "An object of class [`dribble`], a tibble with one row per item." It seems reasonable to mention somewhere that if no items are found, it will return a 0-row tibble (and not error/warn). However, I'm unsure if other functions which use the template share this behavior. It looks to be most (all?) of the functions use this template for the return. What's action would you recommend?



Closes #289

title: build drive_download()
description:
This is a WIP - working out how to best download files from Google Drive.

@jennybc I've changed the philosophy a bit from the first push. Now the user can download a single file using `drive_download()`, which will output an object of class `drive_file` containing the raw data from Google Drive, parsed by httr. 

Note: Right now the code is pretty light because I rely on [httr::content() auto-parsing](https://github.com/r-lib/httr/blob/1fc659856602f60ff75eb01903513244e3491ec2/R/content-parse.r) (which I know is a no-no 😬) - I've linked to how they elect to parse from mime type - I think we should do something similar, but don't want to reinvent the 🎡?

Here is how it would work:
```
chickens <- drive_download("chickwts.csv")
```
Here `chickens` will be a `tibble` with the contents of chickwts.csv.

This will extract the .csv and save it locally to the working directory as "chickens.csv":
```
drive_read_csv("chickwts.csv", path = "chickens.csv")
```

description:
FYI @LucyMcGowan 

My motivation for revisiting the Discovery Document was to retain all the Team Drive endpoints.

But while I was in there I also reworked our treatment of the endpoints that support media upload:

  * create (we wrap in `drive_upload()`
  * update (we wrap in `drive_update()`

I took a slightly different approach: duplicating the base endpoint, then digging the upload URI out of it and elevating it to `path`.

I also removed the resumable upload component because that URI contradicts what I've just read in the Drive media upload docs. If we ever implement resumable upload, someone will have to get to the bottom of that. 

Finally, I sort the endpoints on their name. My hope is that this will lead to more informative diffs in our JSON in the future, when we add endpoints and/or the Discovery Document updates.

title: Accommodate rooted and unrooted paths; closes #60
description:
Another WIP, this one substantially uglier. I'm not exactly sure how (if?) the path handling code can be made much easier to digest.

The main change here is that previously I assumed that `drive_path()` and friends were given a *rooted* path. If it was a filename, I looked for a file by that name in user's top-level My Drive folder. If it was path, I looked for such a path that had top-level My Drive as immediate parent. I think this is too restrictive and not compatible with how Drive usually shows people their stuff. I decided the default assumption should be to find any file or path that is compatible.

Therefore, we need a way to specify a rooted path and I'm now using the `~/whatever` convention for that.

Happy to hear your thoughts. Otherwise I will do some more testing and merge in a bit.

See #60

title: Hello dribble; closes #62, closes #35
description:
This is a sketch of what this should look like. It's just a bare start, but hopefully enough to demonstrate the overall plan.

This creates the dribble class, to the extent that S3 classes really exist! Then defines lots of `as.dribble()` methods to get a dribble from all the obvious inputs. This should be called on all user input that specifies a Drive file and on all output that returns Drive files. The `drive_hello()` function is a toy example so I can make this demo. This function can deal with input that is character (interpreted as path), character marked with `drive_id` class (interpreted as file id), and dribble.

``` r
devtools::load_all(".")
#> Loading googledrive
#> Auto-refreshing stale OAuth token.

drive_hello("Copy of chickwts")
#> Hi, my name is 'Copy of chickwts'!
#> My fileId starts with 1nfpIGA

d <- drive_hello(drive_id("1nfpIGAk97bj43DVmPivo5aFQFne7hWCqHUYSNEcyN7M"))
#> Hi, my name is 'Copy of chickwts'!
#> My fileId starts with 1nfpIGA

drive_hello(d)
#> Hi, my name is 'Copy of chickwts'!
#> My fileId starts with 1nfpIGA
```

title: WIP: re-fashion drive_list() as drive_search() (closes #69 and closes #53)
description:
Existing `drive_list()` was a messy hybrid of path finding, folder listing, searching, and filtering.

Proposal: kill existing `drive_list()`, in favour of a simpler function `drive_search()`. Its job is to do the operations described in the [Search for Files guide](https://developers.google.com/drive/v3/web/search-parameters). All path work should go through `drive_path()`. I've added an example to `drive_search()` for how to list the contents of a folder. We could wrap that nicely in future and call it `drive_list()`.

It is unavoidable to patch up `drive_upload()` because it calls `drive_list()` and it's used in many tests. I've made it dramatically simpler but have left some to do's for you. Can you finish this off so we pass tests again? The goal is to do as little as possible until we straighten out the dribble thing.
